name: Neonatal Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
aliases: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Neonates

criteria.description: Acute onset of respiratory distress within 7 days of a known clinical insult
Bilateral opacities on chest radiograph not fully explained by effusions, lobar/lung collapse, or nodules
Impaired oxygenation defined by oxygenation index or oxygen saturation index thresholds
Respiratory failure not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria including acute onset, bilateral radiographic opacities, and oxygenation impairment plus exclusion of cardiac failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of respiratory distress such as congenital malformations or infections.

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP) if secondary infection present
imaging: Chest X-ray with bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates
Possible ground-glass opacities on lung ultrasound or CT
other: Exclusion of congenital heart disease by echocardiography
Assessment of oxygenation index for severity grading

distinguishingFeatures: Occurs primarily in preterm infants due to surfactant deficiency
Radiographic findings show ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms
Patchy infiltrates with hyperinflation on chest X-ray
Often presents with airway obstruction and air trapping

redFlags: Progressive hypoxemia despite maximal respiratory support
references: De Luca D, et al. The Montreux definition of neonatal ARDS: biological and clinical background. Pediatr Res. 2017.
Khemani RG, et al. Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Definition, Incidence, and Epidemiology. Pediatr Crit Care Med. 2015.
Orphanet: Neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome. ORPHA:217563.
